title: Datasets
text:
All datasets in the current Peekbank release. Each dataset was contributed by the original research team and imported into the common Peekbank format; see the How to Cite page for citation policy — when you use a dataset, cite its original publication (shown here) as well as the database.

manifest = d3.json("slices/manifest.json")







Inputs.table(
  manifest.datasets.map((d) => ({
    dataset: d.name,
    citation: d.cite || d.shortcite,
    children: d.n_subjects,
    sessions: d.n_admins,
    trials: d.n_trials,
    "age range (mo)": `${d.age_min}–${d.age_max}`,
    method: d.methods.join(", "),
    languages: d.languages.join(", "),
    words: d.n_words,
  })),
  { maxHeight: 700, layout: "auto" }
)







html`<p style="color:#6b7280">Release ${manifest.version} ·
${manifest.datasets.length} datasets · generated from the
<a href="https://redivis.com/datapages/datasets/peekbank">peekbank dataset on
Redivis</a>.</p>`

title: About this site
text:
This site provides interactive visualizations of the Peekbank database, an open repository of developmental eye-tracking data from looking-while-listening studies of children’s word recognition.
All plots are computed in your browser from compact per-dataset extracts of the current database release, which is versioned and hosted on Redivis. For full data access use the peekbankr R package, query the dataset directly on Redivis, or see the data access documentation.

title: About this site
text:
The analyses
The visualizations follow the analysis conventions of the original Peekbank Shiny app (Fernald et al., 2008): proportion target looking among target-and-distractor looks; landing-time reaction times on distractor-initial trials; onset-contingent looking curves. Trials excluded by the contributing labs are included by default (Peekbank archives all contributed data), and can be filtered with the “Include lab-excluded trials” toggle.
Built with Quarto and Observable; source at peekbank/peekbank-datapage.

title: Peekbank
text:
What is Peekbank?
The Peekbank project aggregates eye-tracking data from studies of children’s word recognition using the looking-while-listening paradigm: children see two pictures and hear a sentence naming one of them, and their gaze reveals how quickly and accurately they recognize the word. Individual studies are small; pooled in a common format, they let us map the developmental trajectory of word recognition across ages, items, and languages.
This site provides interactive, in-browser visualizations of the current database release. For documentation, data access via the peekbankr R package, and information about contributing a dataset, see the main Peekbank site.
